full_judgment: 7. The petitioner contested the writ petition and filed an affidavit-in-opposition stating that Kalimata temple in question was a holy place for the Hindu community of the whole country and not only of Rangpur, that the land covered by CS Plot No. 4137 is being used as entrance of the said temple for more than 100 years, that easement right has been established on the said land and the land covered by CS Plot No. 4138, although the same was recorded in the Khas Khatian as the acquired land from the Zaminder, that the devotees enjoyed and possessed the same as the adjunct of the temple for the purpose of Puja and other ceremonies from time immemorial since establishment of Deity in the year 1298 BS without any interruption from any quarter and, as such, easement right had accrued in favour of the Deity through adverse possession. The petitioner alleged that the construction of the market by the respondent would not only destroy the security and sanctity of the temple but also the devotees will be in great trouble in entering the temple for performing Puja and Bhog and that the construction of the market caused great hardship to the devotees and the communal harmony in Rangpur was at stake. The petitioner also alleged that the respondent by practising fraud tampered with the volume book of the Sub-Registrar's office by adding some words in the registered deed through illegal means and inserted the word 'shop' after the word house and included the word 'business' after the word 'residence' throughout the said deed. The petitioner also alleged that the respondent upon collecting the certified copy of the lease deed after tampering with the volume book of the Sub-Registrar's office applied for approval of the plan for the said market to the Chairman. Rangpur Paurashava and thus misled the Paurashava by his fraudulent act. The local Administration was not taking effective steps for stopping the construction of the said market by the respondent and so the petitioner was compelled to file an application on 9-12-93 to the Government upon which the Government had issued the impugned order dated 21-12-93 directing to maintain status quo. The Deputy Commissioner, however, due to reasons best known to him did not comply with the Government order and allowed the respondent to continue his illegal construction work. The Government having come to know of this, sent a telex message to implement the order dated 21-12-93 and to submit a report of compliance immediately. The Government by another telex message sent for the record of the settlement case.
